statements.statement: Percent-encode `$ : / ? # [ ] @` in usernames and passwords for portable credentials.
RFC 3986 defines a percent-encoded octet as % followed by two hex digits.
The connection-string spec says drivers should follow RFC 3986 userinfo rules but may accept some reserved characters unencoded for backward compatibility.
statements.note: SHOULD/MAY wording; the exceptions are @ and :, which must stay encoded.

edits.rationale: The Manual says these characters must be percent-encoded. RFC 3986 defines pct-encoded as % plus two hex digits. The connection-string spec says drivers SHOULD require RFC 3986 userinfo encoding but MAY allow reserved characters other than @ and : unencoded for backwards compatibility.

If you aren't able to provide a full list of hosts in the replica set, you can specify one or more of the hosts in the replica set and instruct .NET/C# Driver to perform automatic discovery to find the others.

statements.statement: The Manual says standard connection strings require all cluster members.
The SDAM specification describes discovery from a seed list containing one or more members.
The current .NET/C# guide describes discovery from one or more specified members.

edits.rationale: The Manual says standard connection strings require all cluster members. The SDAM spec requires discovery from a seed list of one or more members, and the .NET/C# guide says you can specify one or more hosts and rely on automatic discovery. The documents therefore differ in emphasis as claimed.
